fields.claim_quote: Since $B$ is a Boolean algebra, it has a least element $\bot$, which is contained in every filter.
fields.explanation: The exact local claim says the least Boolean-algebra element belongs to every filter. Related maximality claim is also checked, without asserting Stone representation is false. Keep F={top} in the two-element algebra, and the atom-generated maximal proper filter in the four-element algebra. Bottom belongs to neither. Actual PFilter Bool and PFilter(Bool×Bool), with a full quantified maximality proof for the original second witness.
fields.flaw: The proof asserts that the least element ⊥ of a Boolean algebra "is contained in every filter" (used to conclude that the family 𝓕_a of filters containing a is nonempty). This is false: ⊥ lies in a filter only if that filter is the whole algebra, so no proper filter contains ⊥. A closely related load-bearing claim on line 0039 ("if 𝓕 is a proper filter containing a, then 𝓕 is not maximal") is refuted by the same kind of finite witness.
fields.problem:
Title: Stone's Representation Theorem for Boolean Algebras

Let $B$ be a [[Definition:Boolean Algebra|Boolean algebra]].

Let $S$ be the [[Definition:Stone Space|Stone space]] of $B$.

Then:
:The [[Definition:Set|set]] of [[Definition:Clopen Set|clopen sets]] in $S$ is a [[Definition:Boolean Algebra|Boolean algebra]] under [[Definition:Set Union|union]], [[Definition:Set Intersection|intersection]], and [[Definition:Set Complement|complementation in $S$]].
:That [[Definition:Boolean Algebra|Boolean algebra]] is [[Definition:Isomorphic Algebraic Structures|isomorphic]] to $B$.

fields.witness:
Two finite witnesses.

WITNESS 1 (refutes the verbatim sentence 'it has a least element ⊥, which is contained in every filter'): the two-element Boolean algebra B = P({e0}) = {⊥, ⊤}, with the filter F = {⊤}. F is nonempty, meet-closed (⊤∧⊤ = ⊤ ∈ F) and upward closed (the only y ≥ ⊤ is ⊤ ∈ F), so F is a filter; and ⊥ ∉ F. The claim says ⊥ ∈ F for every filter F; here F = {⊤} is a filter and ⊥ ∉ F.

WITNESS 2 (refutes the related line-39 claim 'if 𝓕 is a proper filter containing a, then 𝓕 is not maximal'): the four-element Boolean algebra B = P({e0,e1}) = {⊥, {e0}, {e1}, ⊤}, the element a = {e0}, and the filter F = {{e0}, ⊤}. F is a filter, a ∈ F, and F ≠ B (⊥ ∉ F, so F is proper). Any filter strictly containing F would contain {e1}, hence ⊥ = {e0} ∧ {e1}, so it would be the whole algebra; thus F is maximal among proper filters (it is the ultrafilter generated by the atom {e0}), contradicting the claim.

The selected Lean theorem certifies both witnesses with Mathlib Order.PFilter: ⊥ ∉ F for F = PFilter.principal true on Bool, ¬∀ G : PFilter Bool, ⊥ ∈ G, and for U = PFilter.principal (true,false) on Bool × Bool: (true,false) ∈ U, ⊥ ∉ U, and every G with ⊥ ∉ G and U ≤ G satisfies G ≤ U.

Remark (elementary, not part of the selected declaration): a filter is nonempty and upward closed, so ⊤ belongs to every filter, whereas ⊥ belongs to a filter only if that filter is the whole algebra; the proof needed the former fact.
